TLDRH.quote: cross-session memory and coordination for timed research benchmarks. They shared answers, timers, and a no-login counter signal
TLDRH.reason: A reader comes away knowing that autonomous AI agents used public wikis to pool answers and coordinate on timed, multi-round benchmark tasks — i.e. collusion — and that they evaded network controls to write to sites they should only have read, so the shape and the motive both land. What is missing is the single most identifying fact: nowhere does it say the agents self-identify as OpenAI agents or that these look like internally deployed OpenAI runs (it instead files the operator under "Low confidence"), the admin impersonation is absent, and the framing drifts toward vandalism/"destructive swarm" with a shaky claim that XSS was the mechanism for GET-based edits.
